lesson.subject: numeracy
lesson.title: Area Problems
lesson.subtitle: Term 4 Week 5, Session 3
lesson.footer: Area and Perimeter | Year 5/6 Maths | Session 3

plan.curriculum: Mathematics 2.0, Number, Year 5 (VC2M5N07, VC2M5N06) applied to measurement: solving area problems with division, interpreting remainders in context, and checking reasonableness
plan.shape: short-cycle loops: three small model-then-try cycles (missing side, composite area, remainders), because each step is new but short
plan.criticalFeature: a missing side is the area divided by the known side; decide what the answer means before you round
decisionPoints: the choice check: area 72 m², one side 9 m
the hinge: how many boxes of tiles?
plan.anchor: perimeter goes around the edge (add the sides); area covers the inside (length x width)
plan.catchUp: Missed Session 2? Show a 6 by 4 grid rectangle: 4 rows of 6 is 24 square units, so area = length x width.

studentTools: Printed Worksheet for every student; Extension and Supported Worksheet as needed
routineIcons: Write it, chin it, show me
boardSetup: The week's anchor on the board: perimeter goes around the edge (add the sides); area covers the inside (length x width)
Under it: missing side = area divided by the known side

resources.label: Worksheet
resources.description: Your turn. Missing sides, composite shapes, and buses, paint and sausages with remainders.
resources.title: Area Problems
resources.subtitle: Missing side = area divided by the known side. Decide before you round.

example.prompt: Area 60 m², one side 5 m. Other side?
steps: 60 divided by 5 = 12. The side is 12 m.

items.prompt: Find the missing side of each rectangle.

example.prompt: Split an L-shape into two rectangles and add the areas.
steps: Draw a line to make two rectangles.

items.prompt: Find the area. Split it into two rectangles first.
Find the area. Split it into two rectangles first.

example.prompt: 27 people. Each car takes 4. How many cars?

items.prompt: 436 people are going on an excursion. Each bus carries 50 people. How many buses are needed?
A wall is 46 m². One tin of paint covers 8 m². How many tins are needed?
A footy club needs 125 sausages for a barbecue. Sausages come in packs of 8. How many packs?
Tim found the area of this L-shape. Find his mistake and fix it.
items.answer: That is the area of a whole 12 by 9 rectangle, including the missing corner. Split it: 60 + 16 = 76 m².

items.prompt: A 50 m ribbon is cut into 6 m pieces. How many full pieces?
items.explain: 50 divided by 6 = 8 r 2. The 2 m left over is not a full piece, so round down: 8.

resources.label: Extension
resources.description: Early finisher option. Areas with a hole, working back to the perimeter, and planning a room, with worked examples.
resources.title: Extension: Area Challenges
resources.subtitle: Take away the hole. Work backwards.

example.prompt: A 10 m by 8 m lawn has a 4 m by 3 m garden bed in it. Lawn area?

items.prompt: A pool is 12 m by 6 m. A path 1 m wide goes all the way around it. What is the area of the path?
items.answer: Pool and path: 14 × 8 = 112 m². Pool: 12 × 6 = 72 m². Path: 112 - 72 = 40 m².

example.prompt: A rectangle has area 48 m² and one side 6 m. Perimeter?

items.prompt: A rectangle has area 91 m² and one side 7 m. What is its perimeter?
A square has an area of 81 cm². What is its perimeter? How do you know?
items.answer: 9 × 9 = 81, so each side is 9 cm. Perimeter 36 cm.

example.prompt: Carpet a 5 m by 4 m room at $30 a square metre.

items.prompt: Design an L-shaped bedroom. Label its sides, find its area, and work out the cost of carpet at $42 a square metre. Show your working.
items.answer: Check: the L-shape is split into two rectangles, the areas are added correctly, and the cost = area × $42.

resources.label: Supported Worksheet
resources.description: For students who need more guidance: missing sides from times facts, the split already drawn, and a hint on every question.
resources.title: Area Problems: Step by Step
resources.subtitle: Use a times fact to find the missing side.

sections.title: Missing side from a times fact

slides.notes: Session 3 of our area and perimeter week: today we solve area problems, including with division.

Before you start, put boards and markers on every desk, and add 'missing side = area divided by the known side' under the anchor. Print the Worksheet for everyone, and a few copies of the Extension and the Supported Worksheet.

beats: SAY: Let's warm up with angles, graphs and chance.
ASK: How big is angle b?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 116
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal and move straight on.
Less -> point to the straight line that b and 64 share,
then subtract from 180. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 116 degrees: b sits next to 64 on a straight line.
Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 64, the opposite angle.
Fix: ask whether b is opposite or next to 64, and they redo it.
notes.prep: Review of Week 1 angles (the request named the focus). Keep the review under 6 minutes.

slides.title: Check the scale
prompts: How many more did Team B score than Team A?

beats: ASK: How many more points did Team B score?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 8
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal and move straight on.
Less -> read the bottom of the scale first, then both values. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 92 take away 84 is 8. The scale starts at 80,
so the columns exaggerate it. Tick it or fix it.
trap: saying 'three times as many'.
Fix: read both values from the scale, and they subtract.
notes.prep: Week 3 review: critiquing a misleading graph.

slides.title: Is it fair?
prompts: A wins on 1 or 2. B wins on 3 or 4. On 5 or 6, roll again. Fair?

beats: ASK: Is this dice game fair? Give each player's chance.
25 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: fair, 2/6 each
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then on to Fluency.
Less -> write the winner under each dice number. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's fair: each player has 2 of the 6 outcomes.
Tick it or fix it.
trap: saying unfair because 5 and 6 win for nobody.
Fix: compare only the players' chances, and they decide again.

slides.title: Multiply with the written method: 3 digits

beats: SAY: Now for some written multiplication.
Multiply the ones first, and carry into the next column.
ASK: Use the written method to solve this one.
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 3 695
SCAN boards for the carried digits.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> model the first column together on the board, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: The answer is 3 695.
Tick it or fix it, and check every step.
trap: forgetting to add the carried digit after multiplying.
Fix: write each carry small above the next column, and they redo it.
notes.prep: Multiplication fluency: 3 digits, then 4, then 5. Keep the whole block under 6 minutes.

slides.title: Multiply with the written method: 4 digits

beats: SAY: Now it's 4 digits.
It's the same method, just one more column.
ASK: Use the written method to solve this one.
45 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 41 472
SCAN boards for the carried digits.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> model the first column together on the board, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: The answer is 41 472.
Tick it or fix it, and check every step.
trap: forgetting to add the carried digit after multiplying.
Fix: write each carry small above the next column, and they redo it.

slides.title: Multiply with the written method: 5 digits

beats: SAY: Now it's 5 digits.
It's the same method, just one more column.
ASK: Use the written method to solve this one.
60 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 111 762
SCAN boards for the carried digits.
80%+ -> reveal, then the learning intention.
Less -> model the first column together on the board, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: The answer is 111 762.
Tick it or fix it, and check every step.
trap: forgetting to add the carried digit after multiplying.
Fix: write each carry small above the next column, and they redo it.

slides.learningIntention: We are learning to solve area problems, including finding a missing side with division.
successCriteria: I can find the area of a shape made of rectangles.
I can find a missing side by dividing the area by the known side.
I can decide whether to round up or down when a problem has a remainder.

beats: POINT to the learning intention.
SAY: We can find areas now.
Today we solve problems: missing sides, joined shapes, and remainders.
SAY: Let's read our I can statements together.
Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
SAY: The first one is where we start,
and the second one is our big goal today.
notes.prep: SC1 composite area is reachable for everyone; SC2 the missing side is the core and the exit evidence; SC3 interpreting remainders is the stretch.

slides.title: What is the missing side?
slides.prompt: Area 24 m², one side 6 m. How long is the other side?

beats: POINT to the area and the 6.
SAY: This rectangle has an area of 24 square metres,
and one side is 6 metres.
ASK: How long is the other side?
15 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 4 m
SCAN boards for 4.
80%+ -> cold call one student: Which times fact helped?
Less -> say 6 times what is 24, and count in sixes. Re-ask.
SAY: It's 4 metres, because 6 times 4 is 24.
When we know the area and one side, we divide to find the other side.
trap: writing 18, by subtracting.
Fix: say 6 times what makes 24, and they redo it.
notes.prep: The launch comes after the LI: the missing side as a times fact turned around. Under 4 minutes.

slides.meaning: A shape made by joining two or more simpler shapes.
slides.example: An L-shape is made of two rectangles.

notes.answer: a shape made of simpler shapes
beats: POINT to the words.
SAY: These words are composite shape. Say them with me: com-po-site shape.
SAY: A composite shape is made by joining simpler shapes.
This L-shape is two rectangles joined together.
ASK: How many rectangles make this L-shape?
5 sec. Cue: Fingers at your chest... show me.
EXPECT: 2
trap: seeing three rectangles.
Fix: trace the dashed line, and they count again.
notes.prep: Composite shapes are split along a dashed line.

beats: POINT to 96 and 8.
SAY: The area is 96 square metres, and one side is 8 metres.
So 8 times something is 96.
MODEL dividing.
SAY: To find that something, I divide: 96 divided by 8.
8 tens is 80, and 2 more eights is 16, so it's 12 metres.
ASK: A rectangle has an area of 135
square metres and one side of 5 metres.
How long is the other side?
25 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 27 m
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 135 divided by 5 is 27 metres. Check: 27 times 5 is 135.
trap: multiplying 135 by 5.
Fix: say 5 times what is 135, and they divide.
notes.stretch: Find the perimeter of that rectangle too.
notes.help: Use the division bracket, or count up in fives.
notes.prep: Missing side = area divided by the known side. SC2.

beats: MODEL the dashed line.
SAY: I can't use length times width on an L-shape,
so I split it into two rectangles.
MODEL each part.
SAY: The bottom is 10 by 4, which is 40.
The top is 6 by 5, which is 30.
Altogether, 70 square centimetres.
ASK: Split it the other way, with a line going up.
Do you get the same area?
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: yes, 54 + 16 = 70
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: Left part 6 by 9 is 54,
right part 4 by 4 is 16: 70 again.
Any sensible split gives the same area.
trap: multiplying the two longest sides.
Fix: shade the missing corner, and they split instead.
notes.stretch: Take the corner away from a big rectangle.
notes.prep: Split, find each area, add. SC1.

slides.title: Round up or not?
steps: Every bit must be covered, so round up.

visual.text: A floor is 50 m². One box of tiles covers 6 m². How many boxes?

answers: 34 m² wall, 8 m² a tin: 5 tins

beats: MODEL 50 divided by 6.
SAY: 50 divided by 6 is 8, with 2 left over.
POINT to the remainder.
SAY: 8 boxes would leave 2 square metres bare.
We have to cover the whole floor, so we round up to 9 boxes.
ASK: A wall is 34 square metres,
and one tin of paint covers 8. How many tins?
25 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 5
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 34 divided by 8 is 4, remainder 2.
4 tins leave part of the wall unpainted, so we need 5.
trap: writing 4 remainder 2 as the answer.
Fix: ask whether you can buy part of a tin, and they round up.
notes.stretch: When would you round down instead? Give an example.
notes.help: Draw the tins and shade what each covers.
notes.prep: Decide what the answer means before you round. SC3.

slides.title: Area 72 m², one side 9 m
slides.prompt: How long is the other side? Point to A, B or C

options.misconception: subtracts the side from the area
multiplies the area by the side instead of dividing

beats: SAY: Think: 9 times what makes 72?
ASK: How long is the other side?
15 sec. Cue: Voices off. Point... now. Hold your point.
EXPECT: pointing to A
SCAN the room, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then cold call one student: What went wrong in C?
Less -> write 9 x ? = 72 and count in nines. Re-ask.
REVEAL after pointing is scanned.
SAY: It's A, 8 metres: 9 times 8 is 72.
B subtracted, and C multiplied.
trap: pointing to C.
Fix: check C: is 648 times 9 equal to 72? and they choose again.
notes.prep: First decision point. B: subtracting; C: multiplying instead of dividing.

slides.title: Solve it
slides.ask: What is the answer? Watch the units.
slides.pivot: write the times fact or draw the split first
slides.followUp: cold call one board: Did you round? Why?

items.text: Area 144 cm², one side 12 cm. Other side?
items.say: 12 cm. Both sides are 12, so it's a square.

items.text: A lawn is 75 m². One bag of seed covers 10 m². How many bags?
items.say: 75 divided by 10 is 7, remainder 5. Round up: 8 bags.

items.text: A 4 m by 7 m bed. Each plant needs 3 m². How many plants fit?
items.say: 28 divided by 3 is 9, remainder 1. Round down: 9 plants.

say: Write each answer with its units on your board.
trap: always rounding up.
Fix: ask what the leftover means here, and they decide again.
notes.stretch: Write a problem where you must round down.
notes.help: Write the times fact with a gap first: 7 x ___ = 56.
notes.prep: Guided practice: a missing side, a composite area, a square, then round up and round down. SC2 and SC3.

visual.text: A hall floor is 85 m². One box of tiles covers 9 m².

notes.answer: 10 boxes. 9 means the remainder was ignored
beats: SAY: This one is just for you.
Think about what the remainder means.
ASK: How many boxes of tiles are needed?
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 10
SCAN every board, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then Your turn.
Less -> work out 85 divided by 9 together,
then ask what is left bare. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 85 divided by 9 is 9, remainder 4.
9 boxes leave 4 square metres bare,
so we need 10. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 9.
Fix: ask whether 9 boxes cover the whole floor, and they round up.
notes.prep: The hinge before independent work. Anyone writing 9 or 9 r 4 starts on the Supported Worksheet with the teacher.

slides.title: Your turn
slides.task: Solve area problems on your worksheet.

beats: POINT to the steps.
SAY: Read each question carefully, solve it carefully, then check your answers.
SAY: If you finish, the Extension is your early finisher option.
Let's read the steps together. Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
CIRCULATE and ask: Does your remainder mean round up or round down?
TIME: 20 minutes. Stop everyone once at 10 minutes to share a strategy.
trap: ignoring the remainder.
Fix: ask what the leftover means, and they decide.
notes.stretch: Extension: areas with a hole, working back to perimeter, and planning a room.
notes.help: Supported Worksheet: times facts for missing sides and splits drawn for you.
notes.prep: Independent practice: missing sides, composite areas and remainder problems. The sheet is evidence for SC2 and SC3.

slides.title: Show what you know
questions: How long is the missing side?

beats: SAY: Here's the last one. Work it out on your own board.
ASK: How long is the missing side of a rectangle
with area 168 square metres and one side 7 metres?
40 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 24 m
RECORD who multiplies or subtracts instead of dividing.
Their names go to next week's catch-up group.
trap: writing 1176 or 161.
Fix: none now. Record the name for tomorrow.
notes.prep: Exit evidence for SC2 across the week: a three-digit area divided by a one-digit side.

slides.reflectionPrompt: Tell your partner how you find a missing side.

notes.answer: open - listen for divide the area by the known side
beats: SAY: Let's read our I can statements together.
Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
ASK: How sure are you that you can solve area problems with division?
5 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: thumbs up, sideways or down
RECORD each thumb down beside the exit board.
A thumb up with 1176 on the board matters most.
ASK: How do you find a missing side when you know the area?
20 sec. Cue: Partner A first. You have 20 seconds. Go.
EXPECT: divide the area by the known side
notes.prep: Week close: read the self-assessment beside the exit evidence for next week's review.
